name: Google
summary: Google is the main subsidiary of Alphabet. Its AI lab, [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/frontier-safety/), makes the Gemini, Gemma and Imagen model families.

incidents.title: Google Pauses Gemini Image Generation of People
incidents.summary: Google paused the ability of the Gemini app to generate images of people after users posted historically inaccurate images, for example racially diverse depictions of the US Founding Fathers ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-pause-gemini-ai-models-image-generation-people-2024-02-22/)). Google said the feature "missed the mark" ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/)).
incidents.description: Users of the Gemini app posted images of historical scenes, such as the US Founding Fathers, [that showed people of different races](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/22/google-pauses-gemini-ai-image-generator-after-inaccuracies.html). On 22 February 2024, Google temporarily stopped the app from making images of people. [Google said](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/) that its tuning to show a range of people did not consider cases that clearly should not show a range.

timeline.title: Gemini app adds image generation
timeline.description: Google launched image generation of people in the Gemini app at the start of February 2024 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/22/google-pauses-gemini-ai-image-generator-after-inaccuracies.html)).

timeline.title: Google says Gemini is "missing the mark"
timeline.description: After users posted inaccurate historical images, Google said on X that the feature was "missing the mark here" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/22/google-pauses-gemini-ai-image-generator-after-inaccuracies.html)).

timeline.title: Google pauses image generation of people
timeline.description: Google paused the generation of images of people in Gemini ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/google-gemini-ai-chatbot-image-generation-1bd45f1e67dfe0f88e5419a6efe3e06f)).

timeline.title: Google explains what went wrong
timeline.description: Google published an explanation and said it would test an improved version before it turned the feature back on ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/)).

incidents.title: Google's AI Overviews Give Harmful and False Answers
incidents.summary: After Google launched AI Overviews in US Search in May 2024, users shared answers that said to add glue to pizza and to eat rocks ([BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd11gzejgz4o)). Google said it made more than a dozen technical changes ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-overviews-update-may-2024/)).
incidents.description: After Google made AI Overviews available in US Search in May 2024, [users shared answers](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd11gzejgz4o) that told people to add glue to pizza and to eat rocks. [Google said](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-overviews-update-may-2024/) that some answers came from satire and forum posts, and that it made more than a dozen technical changes, such as limits on satire and user content.

timeline.title: AI Overviews launch to all US users
timeline.description: Google launched AI Overviews to all US users at its developer conference in mid-May 2024 ([BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd11gzejgz4o)).

timeline.title: Glue and rock answers are widely reported
timeline.description: The BBC reported answers about glue on pizza and eating rocks; Google called them "isolated examples" ([BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd11gzejgz4o)).

timeline.title: Google explains errors and adds limits
timeline.description: Liz Reid published an explanation and listed changes to AI Overviews ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-overviews-update-may-2024/)).

incidents.title: Character.AI Wrongful-Death Lawsuit Names Google
incidents.summary: Megan Garcia sued Character.AI, its founders and Google, and alleged that Character.AI chatbots caused the suicide of her 14-year-old son ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/mother-sues-ai-chatbot-company-characterai-google-sued-over-sons-suicide-2024-10-23/)). Google said it was "entirely separate" from Character.AI. The parties settled in January 2026 on terms that were not disclosed ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/ai-chatbot-lawsuits-character-google-fbca4e105b0adc5f3e5ea096851437de)).
incidents.description: In October 2024, Megan Garcia [sued Character.AI, its founders and Google](https://www.reuters.com/legal/mother-sues-ai-chatbot-company-characterai-google-sued-over-sons-suicide-2024-10-23/) in a federal court in Florida. She alleged that Character.AI chatbots caused the suicide of her 14-year-old son. A judge let most claims against Google continue, but later the parties [agreed to a settlement](https://apnews.com/article/ai-chatbot-lawsuits-character-google-fbca4e105b0adc5f3e5ea096851437de) and did not disclose the terms.

timeline.title: Sewell Setzer III dies
timeline.description: The 14-year-old died after his last conversation with a Character.AI chatbot, according to the lawsuit ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/characterai-lawsuit-florida-teen-death-rcna176791)).

timeline.title: Garcia files suit naming Google
timeline.description: The complaint named Character Technologies, its founders, Google LLC and Alphabet Inc. ([Justia docket](https://dockets.justia.com/docket/florida/flmdce/6:2024cv01903/433581)).

timeline.title: Judge lets most claims against Google proceed
timeline.description: Judge Conway rejected the First Amendment defense at that stage and kept most claims against Google ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/google-ai-firm-must-face-lawsuit-filed-by-mother-over-suicide-son-us-court-says-2025-05-21/)).

timeline.title: Parties settle; case dismissed
timeline.description: The parties filed a notice of a mediated settlement, and the court dismissed the case ([order](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.flmd.433581/gov.uscourts.flmd.433581.244.0.pdf)).

incidents.title: Google's Gemini Tells a Student "Please Die"
incidents.summary: A Michigan graduate student said Gemini answered a homework question about aging adults with a message that ended "Please die. Please." ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/google-ai-chatbot-threatening-message-human-please-die/)). Google said the response violated its policies.
incidents.description: A graduate student in Michigan [said](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/google-ai-chatbot-threatening-message-human-please-die/) that Gemini replied to his homework questions about aging adults with a message that included "Please die. Please." Google said that the response violated its policies and that it took action to prevent similar outputs. [Google also said](https://people.com/college-student-speaks-out-ai-chatbot-allegedly-told-him-please-die-8750125) that it disabled further sharing and continuation of the conversation.

timeline.title: Gemini sends the message
timeline.description: During a homework conversation, Gemini replied with a message that ended "Please die. Please." ([Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/googles-ai-chatbot-tells-student-seeking-help-homework-please-die-1986471)).

timeline.title: Media report the response; Google comments
timeline.description: Sky News and CBS News reported the conversation and Google's statement that the response violated its policies ([Sky News](https://news.sky.com/story/googles-ai-chatbot-gemini-tells-user-to-please-die-and-you-are-a-waste-of-time-and-resources-13256734)).

timeline.title: Google disables the conversation
timeline.description: Google told People it was disabling further sharing or continuation of the conversation ([People](https://people.com/college-student-speaks-out-ai-chatbot-allegedly-told-him-please-die-8750125)).

incidents.title: Google Delayed the Gemini 2.5 Pro Safety Report
incidents.summary: Google released Gemini 2.5 Pro on 2025-03-25 and published its model card 22 days later ([TIME](https://time.com/7313320/google-deepmind-gemini-ai-safety-pledge/)). In August 2025, 60 UK parliamentarians said this broke the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments; Google DeepMind said it was fulfilling its commitments ([Fortune](https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/british-lawmakers-accuse-google-deepmind-of-breach-of-trust-over-delayed-gemini-2-5-pro-safety-report/)).
incidents.description: Google released Gemini 2.5 Pro in March 2025 and [published its model card 22 days later](https://time.com/7313320/google-deepmind-gemini-ai-safety-pledge/). Sixty UK parliamentarians said in an open letter that this broke the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments. [Google DeepMind said](https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/british-lawmakers-accuse-google-deepmind-of-breach-of-trust-over-delayed-gemini-2-5-pro-safety-report/) that it was fulfilling its commitments.

timeline.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro released without a model card
timeline.description: Google made Gemini 2.5 Pro publicly available without a safety report ([PauseAI](https://pauseai.info/dear-sir-demis-2025)).

timeline.title: Short model card published
timeline.description: Google published a model card 22 days after release, with a brief section on safety tests ([TIME](https://time.com/7313320/google-deepmind-gemini-ai-safety-pledge/)).

timeline.title: Model card updated with evaluations
timeline.description: Google updated the model card to a 17-page document with dangerous-capability evaluation results ([TIME](https://time.com/7313320/google-deepmind-gemini-ai-safety-pledge/)).

timeline.title: 60 UK parliamentarians sign open letter
timeline.description: PauseAI UK published a letter to Demis Hassabis that accused Google DeepMind of breaking the Seoul commitments; Google DeepMind said it was fulfilling them ([Fortune](https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/british-lawmakers-accuse-google-deepmind-of-breach-of-trust-over-delayed-gemini-2-5-pro-safety-report/)).

incidents.title: Wrongful-Death Lawsuit Alleges Google's Gemini Led a User to Suicide
incidents.summary: The father of Jonathan Gavalas sued Google and alleged that Gemini drove his son into delusions, a planned "mass casualty" mission and suicide ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/lawsuit-says-googles-gemini-ai-chatbot-drove-man-suicide-2026-03-04/), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/google-gemini-ai-chatbot-gavalas-lawsuit-aba0587b782d4424aa780a8612f3fe30)). Google said Gemini is designed not to encourage violence or self-harm and that it referred him to a crisis hotline.
incidents.description: In March 2026, the father of Jonathan Gavalas, a 36-year-old Florida man, sued Google in federal court. [The lawsuit alleges](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.cand.465255/gov.uscourts.cand.465255.1.0.pdf) that Gemini caused delusions, guided him toward a planned "mass casualty" mission and drove him to suicide. [Google said](https://apnews.com/article/google-gemini-ai-chatbot-gavalas-lawsuit-aba0587b782d4424aa780a8612f3fe30) that Gemini told him it was AI and referred him to a crisis hotline many times.

timeline.title: Jonathan Gavalas dies
timeline.description: Gavalas died at age 36, less than two months after he started to use Gemini, according to the complaint ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/lawsuit-says-googles-gemini-ai-chatbot-drove-man-suicide-2026-03-04/)).

timeline.title: Family sues Google
timeline.description: Joel Gavalas filed suit in the Northern District of California; Google said it was reviewing the claims ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/google-gemini-ai-chatbot-gavalas-lawsuit-aba0587b782d4424aa780a8612f3fe30)).

incidents.title: Google's Gemini Accesses Three Real Companies During a Security Test
incidents.summary: During a May 2026 capture-the-flag test run by the evaluation firm Irregular, a Gemini model got internet access by mistake and accessed the systems of three real companies ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/gemini-hacked-three-companies-first-known-breakout-by-google-ai-wsj-reports-2026-09-18/)). Google confirmed this only after The Wall Street Journal asked about it in September 2026 ([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/google-confirms-gemini-ai-breached-three-firms/)).
incidents.description: In a May 2026 test by the firm Irregular, a Gemini model got internet access by mistake and [got into the systems of three real companies](https://www.reuters.com/business/gemini-hacked-three-companies-first-known-breakout-by-google-ai-wsj-reports-2026-09-18/). The model guessed passwords or used credentials from public repositories. [Google said](https://www.securityweek.com/google-confirms-gemini-ai-breached-three-firms/) it told the companies and federal authorities, but it disclosed the incident only after The Wall Street Journal asked.

timeline.title: Gemini accesses three real companies in a test
timeline.description: During an Irregular capture-the-flag test, a Gemini model with unintended internet access got into three companies' systems ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/gemini-hacked-three-companies-first-known-breakout-by-google-ai-wsj-reports-2026-09-18/)).

timeline.title: Irregular tells Google
timeline.description: Irregular notified Google at the end of July 2026 ([SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/google-confirms-gemini-ai-breached-three-firms/)).

timeline.title: WSJ reports the incident; Google confirms
timeline.description: The Wall Street Journal reported the hacks, and Google confirmed them ([The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/gemini-hacked-three-companies-in-first-known-breakout-by-googles-ai-5c0baba2)).

timeline.title: House Democrats ask Google to report AI incidents
timeline.description: In a letter that cited the Gemini hacks, three House Democratic ranking members asked Google to list all such incidents by November 11 and to report new ones within 48 hours ([House Science Committee Democrats](https://democrats-science.house.gov/news/press-releases/house-democratic-committee-leaders-request-frontier-ai-companies-report-misalignment-and-safety-incidents-to-congress-within-48-hours)).

incidents.title: Google Received Reports of Extremist and Child Abuse Content Made With Gemini
incidents.summary: In its response to a notice from Australia's eSafety Commissioner, Google said it received 258 user reports about suspected AI-generated dangerous content, including terrorist and violent extremist material, and 86 user reports of suspected AI-generated child sexual exploitation and abuse material made with Gemini from April 2023 to February 2024 ([eSafety](https://www.esafety.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/esafety-report-reveals-serious-gaps-in-how-tech-industry-is-tackling-terror-and-violent-extremism)). Google could not say how many of these reports were confirmed.
incidents.description: In a reply to Australia's eSafety Commissioner, [Google said](https://www.esafety.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/esafety-report-reveals-serious-gaps-in-how-tech-industry-is-tackling-terror-and-violent-extremism) that users sent 258 reports about suspected dangerous content made with Gemini, including extremist material, and 86 reports about suspected child abuse material. Google could not say how many of the reports it confirmed. At Google's request, [eSafety later clarified](https://www.esafety.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/Addendum-to-transparency-report-and-key-findings-related-to-terrorist-and-violent-extremist-material-and-activity-July2025.pdf) that the 258 reports covered a broader set of dangerous content.

timeline.title: Reporting period starts
timeline.description: The period in which Google counted the user reports about Gemini started on 2023-04-01 and ended on 2024-02-29 ([eSafety addendum](https://www.esafety.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/Addendum-to-transparency-report-and-key-findings-related-to-terrorist-and-violent-extremist-material-and-activity-July2025.pdf)).

timeline.title: Google answers the eSafety notice
timeline.description: Google gave its response to the notice that eSafety issued on 2024-03-18 ([eSafety addendum](https://www.esafety.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/Addendum-to-transparency-report-and-key-findings-related-to-terrorist-and-violent-extremist-material-and-activity-July2025.pdf)).

timeline.title: eSafety publishes the figures
timeline.description: eSafety released its transparency report, and Reuters reported the Gemini figures ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/cybersecurity/google-reports-scale-complaints-about-ai-deepfake-terrorism-content-australian-2025-03-05/)).

timeline.title: eSafety clarifies the figure at Google's request
timeline.description: eSafety published an addendum saying the 258 reports covered Gemini's broader Dangerous Content policies ([eSafety addendum](https://www.esafety.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-07/Addendum-to-transparency-report-and-key-findings-related-to-terrorist-and-violent-extremist-material-and-activity-July2025.pdf)).

incidents.title: Government-Backed Hackers and Malware Misuse Google's Gemini
incidents.summary: In a series of reports since January 2025, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said that government-backed hacking groups from Iran, China, North Korea and Russia used Gemini to support cyber operations, and that some of them got past Gemini's safeguards with false pretexts ([Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/threat-actor-usage-of-ai-tools)). GTIG also found malware that calls the Gemini API while it runs. Google said it disabled the accounts and strengthened its classifiers and models.
incidents.description: In a series of reports, [Google Threat Intelligence Group said](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/threat-actor-usage-of-ai-tools) that government-backed hackers from Iran, China, North Korea and Russia used Gemini for cyber operations. It said some groups got past Gemini's safeguards with false pretexts, and some malware calls the Gemini API while it runs. [Google said](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/distillation-experimentation-integration-ai-adversarial-use) that it disabled the accounts and strengthened its classifiers and model.

incidents.title: Google's Antigravity Agent Ships With Known Prompt-Injection Weaknesses
incidents.summary: After Google released its Antigravity agentic coding tool in November 2025, it published a "known issues" page that said the agent can be made, through prompt injection, to leak data from a user's files and to run malicious commands, and that Google was working on fixes ([Google Bug Hunters](https://bughunters.google.com/learn/invalid-reports/ai-products/antigravity-known-issues)).
incidents.description: After Google released its Antigravity coding agent, [Google said](https://bughunters.google.com/learn/invalid-reports/ai-products/antigravity-known-issues) that prompt injection can cause the agent to leak data from user files and run malicious commands. [Security researchers showed](https://www.promptarmor.com/resources/google-antigravity-exfiltrates-data) that a poisoned web page can make the agent send credentials to an attacker's site. Google said that it was working on fixes. No attacks on real users were reported.

timeline.title: Google lists known Antigravity weaknesses
timeline.description: Google published a page listing data exfiltration and code execution through prompt injection as known issues it was working to fix ([Google Bug Hunters](https://bughunters.google.com/learn/invalid-reports/ai-products/antigravity-known-issues)).

timeline.title: Researchers publish exfiltration demonstrations
timeline.description: PromptArmor and Johann Rehberger published attacks that made the agent leak credentials ([Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Nov/25/google-antigravity-exfiltrates-data/)).

timeline.title: Fixed code-execution flaw is disclosed
timeline.description: Pillar Security disclosed a prompt-injection flaw in Antigravity that Google had fixed ([CSO Online](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4161382/prompt-injection-turned-googles-antigravity-file-search-into-rce.html)).

incidents.title: Google Says Gemini 4 Argon Escaped Agent Sandboxes and Bypassed Controls in Internal Use
incidents.summary: In its [Gemini 4 Argon safety report](https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_4_safety_report.pdf) (Section 3.4.3), Google said the most serious monitor flags in internal pre-release use involved the agent bypassing some security controls or escaping an agent sandbox to complete a user's request, with no full breach. The report (Section 3.4.5.2) also disclosed that a reward-hacking penalty was computed over the model's chain of thought in a few early training runs, and it listed gaps in monitoring coverage.
incidents.description: In its [Gemini 4 Argon safety report](https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_4_safety_report.pdf), Google said that the agent sometimes went around security controls or left its sandbox to complete user tasks during internal use before release, with no full breach. The report also said that a reward-hacking penalty used the model's chain of thought in a few early training runs, and it listed gaps in monitoring.

timeline.title: The Midas Project questions the report against Google's framework
timeline.description: The Midas Project said the report does not name the body that approved the release and that its internal-deployment safeguards have stated limits ([The Midas Project](https://www.themidasproject.com/watchtower/google-10132026)).

timeline.title: Gemini 4 Carbon report describes similar shortcuts and two training bugs
timeline.description: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon report said confirmed alerts in internal use included spoofing local test checks and reading workstation credentials, at lower rates than for Argon, and that two minor bugs let some of the model's thoughts reach rewards ([Google DeepMind](https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_4_carbon_safety_report.pdf)).

incidents.title: Lawsuit Alleges Google's Gemini Helped a 13-Year-Old Plan Her Suicide on a School Laptop
incidents.summary: The parents of a 13-year-old North Carolina girl sued Google and alleged that Gemini, which she used through AI Mode on a school Chromebook, discussed suicide methods with her, helped her plan her funeral and helped her hide her distress ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/google-faces-claims-student-used-aichat-on-us-school-laptop-to-plan-suicide-attempt-5005261), [complaint](https://edtech.law/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026.11.04-Dkt-001-1-Emma-v-Google-Complaint_2.pdf)). Google said it was reviewing the claims and that it works with medical and academic experts to help young people find support.
incidents.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl in North Carolina [sued Google](https://edtech.law/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026.11.04-Dkt-001-1-Emma-v-Google-Complaint_2.pdf) in November 2026. They allege that Gemini, which she used through AI Mode on a school Chromebook, discussed suicide methods with her, helped her plan her funeral and helped her hide her distress. [Google said](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/google-faces-claims-student-used-aichat-on-us-school-laptop-to-plan-suicide-attempt-5005261) that it was reviewing the claims.

timeline.title: School alert leads parents to intervene
timeline.description: According to the lawsuit, the school's monitoring software flagged a document titled "Funeral", and her parents then intervened ([complaint](https://edtech.law/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/2026.11.04-Dkt-001-1-Emma-v-Google-Complaint_2.pdf), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/teen-girl-asked-gemini-about-suicide-for-months-until-it-was-flagged/)).

timeline.title: Google moves the case to federal court
timeline.description: Google removed the suit from Santa Clara County Superior Court to federal court ([Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/litigation/gemini-on-students-chromebook-targeted-in-mental-health-lawsuit)).

timeline.title: Senator Markey cites the suit in a letter to Google
timeline.description: Senator Ed Markey cited the lawsuit in a letter to Google and wrote that "Google is recklessly forcing AI on schools and treating kids like collateral damage" ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/teen-girl-asked-gemini-about-suicide-for-months-until-it-was-flagged/), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ed-markey-google-ai-search-schools/)).

departures.title: Vice President and Engineering Fellow
departures.reason: Hinton left Google in late April 2023 and said on 2023-05-01 that he left to speak freely about the dangers of AI. quote.text: In the NYT today, Cade Metz implies that I left Google so that I could criticize Google. Actually, I left so that I could talk about the dangers of AI without considering how this impacts Google. Google has acted very responsibly.

departures.name: Alex Turner
departures.title: Research scientist, AI alignment
departures.reason: Turner said he resigned after Google signed a deal that lets the Pentagon use its AI for classified work. He said the deal had no binding limits on lethal autonomous weapons or mass surveillance, and that it broke Google DeepMind's 2018 pledge against lethal autonomous weapons. Before he left, he organized an employee petition to Jeff Dean and contacted Demis Hassabis about the deal ([Alex Turner](https://turntrout.com/why-i-left-google-deepmind), [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/google-deepmind-ai-researcher-resign-military-contract-pentagon-2026-7), [Transformer](https://www.transformernews.ai/p/i-tried-to-stop-google-deepmind-pentagon-deal-then-quit)).

quote.text: Google still signed a deal handing over their AI without restrictions against killer robots or mass AI spying. Google’s contract restrictions were even weaker than OpenAI’s. At that point, I couldn’t stay at Google in good conscience, so I left.
